\chapter{Grandparents, and Which Side}
\label{ch:hi-grandparents}
\hlchaptermodality{116}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name my four grandparents and my father's younger brother, and say which side of the family each is on.}

Complete HI-C116-chacha: introduce the family, side by side.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dādā]{\hi{दादा} (dādā) — grandfather, the father's father}

\label{lesson:HI-C116-dada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for by all means, then the Hindi for a polite no.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दादा}}
\textbf{\hi{दादा}} (\emph{dādā}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandfather\textquotedblright{}, your FATHER's father.

English has one word for both grandfathers; Hindi has two, and says which side of the family you mean. \textbf{\hi{मेरे} \hi{दादा}} — \textquotedblleft{}my grandfather\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful plural \textbf{\hi{मेरे}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A grandfather, on your father's side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mere dādā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for by all means, then the Hindi for a polite no, then say \emph{dādā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{दादा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grandfather, the father's father\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dādī]{\hi{दादी} (dādī) — grandmother, the father's mother}

\label{lesson:HI-C116-dadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a polite no, then the Hindi for the father's father.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दादी}}
\textbf{\hi{दादी}} (\emph{dādī}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandmother\textquotedblright{}, your father's mother.

It pairs with \textbf{\hi{दादा}}: the \textbf{-\hi{ई}} ending marks the woman, as in \textbf{\hi{बच्ची}} beside \textbf{\hi{बच्चा}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The father's side, both grandparents.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mere dādā aur merī dādī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a polite no, then the Hindi for the father's father, then say \emph{dādī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{दादी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grandmother, the father's mother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nānā]{\hi{नाना} (nānā) — grandfather, the mother's father}

\label{lesson:HI-C116-nana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for the father's father, then the Hindi for the father's mother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{नाना}}
\textbf{\hi{नाना}} (\emph{nānā}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandfather\textquotedblright{}, your MOTHER's father.

So \textbf{\hi{दादा}} and \textbf{\hi{नाना}} are both \textquotedblleft{}grandfather\textquotedblright{} in English, and never the same man in Hindi.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A grandfather, on your mother's side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mere nānā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for the father's father, then the Hindi for the father's mother, then say \emph{nānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{नाना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grandfather, the mother's father\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nānī]{\hi{नानी} (nānī) — grandmother, the mother's mother}

\label{lesson:HI-C116-nani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for the father's mother, then the Hindi for the mother's father.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{नानी}}
\textbf{\hi{नानी}} (\emph{nānī}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandmother\textquotedblright{}, your mother's mother.

\textbf{\hi{नानी} \hi{का} \hi{घर}} — \textquotedblleft{}grandmother's house\textquotedblright{}, the mother's family home, where many summer holidays are spent.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
All four grandparents, each with a name of their own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nānī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nānī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nānī kā ghar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for the father's mother, then the Hindi for the mother's father, then say \emph{nānī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{नानी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grandmother, the mother's mother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cācā]{\hi{चाचा} (cācā) — uncle, the father's younger brother}

\label{lesson:HI-C116-chacha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for the mother's father, then the Hindi for the mother's mother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चाचा}}
\textbf{\hi{चाचा}} (\emph{cācā}) — \textquotedblleft{}uncle\textquotedblright{}, your father's younger brother.

Like the grandparents, an uncle's name says whose brother he is. \textbf{\hi{मेरे} \hi{चाचा}} — \textquotedblleft{}my uncle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Four grandparents and an uncle: the family says which side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cācā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cācā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mere cācā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for the mother's father, then the Hindi for the mother's mother, then say \emph{cācā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चाचा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Uncle, the father's younger brother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
